summary: Lati Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Ganden Shartse Monastery (earning his Geshe Lharampa by 1959) and Gyuto Monastery, he served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (~1976–1984) and visited the University of Virginia (1976).

Latika Lahiri was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University in 1958 under supervisor Xianlin Ji as an Indian Government scholar and later served on the faculty at the University of Delhi from circa 1969 to 1988.

Laura Harrington works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under instructors including Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., and Gary A. Tubb, and held an attested post at Boston University in 2013.

Laura Massetti is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned her PhD from the University of Cologne (2012–2016). She held research posts at Copenhagen, Oxford, and the Center for Hellenic Studies before joining the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2022–2025).

Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who held teaching posts at Indiana University Bloomington and Rutgers University (attested 2003). At Columbia University (attested 2026), she serves as Adjunct Assistant Professor in Tibetan Literature and Director of the Modern Tibetan Studies Program.

Lauren Bausch specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied under Luis González-Reimann and serves as an Assistant Professor at Dharma Realm Buddhist University (attested 2019–2026).

Laurence Austine Waddell was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. A Glasgow medical graduate, he served as an Indian Medical Service officer, Professor of Chemistry and Pathology at Calcutta Medical College (1896), and Professor of Tibetan at UCL (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology educated at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Keeper of Oriental Prints and Drawings at the British Museum (1915–1933) and held professorships at Harvard (1933–1934) and Athens (1940–1941).

Laurence Khantipalo Mills was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under teachers including Sangharakshita, Chien Ming Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, Namkhai Norbu, and Dudjom Rinpoche. In 1978, he served as the abbot of Wat Buddha Dhamma.

Laurent Van Cutsem specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a BA at Université libre de Bruxelles, an MA at Catholic University of Louvain, and a doctorate at Ghent University (2015–2023), where he became Doctor-Assistant (2023–2026).

Laurentios Myriantheus was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Rizarios Ecclesiastical School and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich, where he studied under Martin Haug and Wilhelm von Christ.

Laurie L. Patton is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago. She held professorships at Bard, Emory, and Duke, and served as President of Middlebury College (2015–2024) and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (~2023).

Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she studies under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Lavanya Vemsani is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies who studied at Osmania University and McMaster University (1999–2004). She became Distinguished University Professor of History at Shawnee State University (~2006) and co-founded the American Academy of Indic Studies.

Lawrence Cohen is an Indologist who completed a Doctor of Pharmacy at USC. He was Professor and Chair at Washington State University (2002–2012) and Distinguished Professor at UNT Health Science Center (2021), and is Professor and Department Chair at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He served as a Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as a Professor in the Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Epstein is a Tibetologist who completed medical studies at UCLA, George Washington University, VA West Los Angeles Medical Center, and Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. He served as an Assistant Professor at the University of Washington (attested 1999–2001).

Lawrence Heyworth Mills was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at NYU, Virginia Theological Seminary, University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Oxford (M.A.), where he was appointed Professor in 1897.

Lawrence J. McCrea specializes in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied under Sheldon Pollock and taught at the University of Chicago (attested 2003) and Harvard University (attested 2004) before becoming a Professor at Cornell University (attested 2026).

Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. His education includes studies at several institutions, culminating in a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies.
